newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open S5 lower Tuesday after early gains overnight on the London market were erased, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures slipped from early highs and traded mostly a touch lower at midday Tuesday. September was off one stg at 1,021 stg a tonne, traded 1,030 to 1,020 stg. December was off the same at 1,052 stg.
Traders said a stronger dollar against the British pound and other European currencies was expected to weigh on the New York market.

Monday, New York cocoa ended broadly higher, boosted by speculative and trade buying. Spot September settled up $15 at $1,496 a tonne after ranging between $1,500 and $1,475. December ended up the same at $1,536, traded $1,538 to $1,515, with the back months $15 to $18 higher.
On the charts, traders said December faced support near $1,526 to $1,528, with the subsequent levels put at $1,518 and $1,510. Resistance was seen at $1,538, followed by $1,548 to $1,550.
